request: Add an `is_valid_email` function to lnbits/helpers.py and use it to validate email in account updates.

summary.result_text:
I added `is_valid_email` and switched account validation to use it. I haven't run any tests: `make test-unit` needed your approval, and I didn't run it.

**What changed**
- `lnbits/helpers.py`: added `is_valid_email(email: str) -> bool`. It requires a dotted domain with a TLD and a length of at most 254 characters.
- `lnbits/core/models/users.py`: `Account.validate_fields()` now calls `is_valid_email`. That method runs on account updates and creation in `lnbits/core/services/users.py` and `lnbits/core/views/user_api.py`.

**Existing name:** The repo already imports `is_valid_email_address` from `lnbits.helpers` in `auth_api.py`, `notifications.py` and `tests/unit/test_helpers.py`, but nothing defines it. I added `is_valid_email_address = is_valid_email` in `helpers.py` so those imports resolve. If you'd rather have a single name, I can rename the other callers and the tests to `is_valid_email` and drop the alias.

**Not verified:** The regex is my own, since there was no existing definition to copy. `tests/unit/test_helpers.py` expects `alice@example.com` to pass and `alice@example` to fail, and the regex should satisfy both, but I haven't run it.

To check it, run `make test-unit`, or approve it and I'll run it.

input.command: git status --short && git log --oneline -3 && sed -n 140,175p tests/unit/test_helpers.py && grep -n "email" lnbits/core/views/auth_api.py | head -30

sed -n 445,475p lnbits/core/views/auth_api.py; grep -n "email\|validate_fields" lnbits/core/views/user_api.py lnbits/core/services/users.py | head -20; sed -n 205,225p lnbits/core/services/notifications.py

grep -n "^test-unit" -A3 Makefile; sed -n 8,16p lnbits/core/models/users.py; poetry run pytest tests/unit/test_helpers.py -q 2>&1 | tail -8 || uv run pytest tests/unit/test_helpers.py -q 2>&1 | tail -8
